body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Monday, August 24, 2026, and we’re starting the week with a high near 105° and air quality at a moderate 63. Overnight, a violent dispute at a wellness facility in southwest Bakersfield made headlines, and we’re tracking one active fire in Kern County. Let’s get you caught up on the news, the night, the weather, and what’s coming up this week.

## The Kern Overnight

Overnight, police and fire crews handled several notable incidents across Bakersfield and Kern County. Just before 11 p.m., officers responded to a wellness facility on Evanston Court in southwest Bakersfield after a dispute escalated, with a roommate reportedly pouring hot water on another resident and on bedding and equipment at the scene. Earlier, around 9:20 p.m., a brush fire was reported in a field in unincorporated Kern County, possibly being put out by residents before fire officials dispatched multiple engines, two battalions, and dozers to the scene. Shortly after 11 p.m., officers also responded to a domestic call on Riverlakes Drive in southwest Bakersfield, where residents were pushing and throwing property; a woman on scene reported she was pregnant and had been struck. About 5:54 a.m., a caller reported that a subject who had just fled had burglarized his residence in north Bakersfield, and officers were investigating. Just after midnight, officers checked on a 19-year-old woman at a residence on Beardsley Avenue in southeast Bakersfield who was under the influence and had made suicidal statements. Overnight activity clustered on the southwest side of town, while the county brush fire was reported to be largely under control by residents before crews arrived.

## Today's weather

Today’s weather will bring a high near 105° and a low around 75° tonight. It’s currently 75° at Meadows Field (KBFL). No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County, and air quality is moderate at an AQI of 63. Fire crews are currently on one active fire in Kern County: the Alper Fire.

## Top stories

**According to Bakersfield Now, a 15-year-old has been arrested in connection with a deadly shooting at an Independence High School football game.** The incident has shaken the community, and the arrest was made miles away from the scene. Meanwhile, **Bakersfield Now also reports that a 26-year-old man was shot and killed at a McFarland laundromat, with no arrest made yet.** The shooting occurred at the Capri Laundromat on Perkins Avenue, and preliminary information indicates two unknown suspects confronted the victim inside the laundromat before fleeing the area. **23ABC reports that McFarland police are investigating the fatal shooting at the Capri Laundromat, where the victim was found suffering from multiple gunshot wounds.** Officers provided medical aid and initiated CPR, but the victim was pronounced dead at the scene. No suspects have been identified, and the motive remains unknown. **KGET 17 reports that Bakersfield Mayor Karen Goh has released a statement on the deadly shooting at Independence High School, addressing community concerns and emphasizing the city’s commitment to safety.**

## Something good

On a brighter note, Cal State Bakersfield has launched its first mariachi ensemble, a cultural and musical milestone for the university. This new ensemble will provide students with an opportunity to learn and perform traditional Mexican music, enriching the campus community.

## Coming up this week

Looking ahead, the Fox Theater has a busy week of events. On Tuesday, August 24, you can catch the Cults & Classics: Season Pass 2026-2027. On Friday, August 27, comedian Rodney Carrington takes the stage. Saturday, August 28, brings the CUMBIATRON: THE CUMBIA RAVE. And on Sunday, August 29, enjoy performances by Willie Barcena and the Michael Return Of The King Tribute Featuring Michael Phoenix. Also on Sunday, the MI HISTORIA TOUR LEYENDAS DEL MARIACHI USA comes to the Fox. On the civic side, the Bakersfield City Council has a special meeting on Thursday, August 26, at 12:00 p.m., followed by a regular City Council Meeting at 3:30 p.m. and another at 5:15 p.m.
